messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Mitochondrial diseases are certain rare inherited metabolic disorders.
Stop taking metformin and call your healthcare professional immediately if you have any symptoms of lactic acidosis, including if you feel:
very weak and tired
have unusual (not normal) muscle pain
have trouble breathing
have unusual sleepiness or sleep longer than usual
have unexplained stomach or intestinal problems with nausea and vomiting, or diarrhea
cold, especially in your arms and legs
dizzy or lightheaded
have a slow or irregular heartbeat
Other warnings:
Vitamin B12 deficiency: Metformin can lower your vitamin B12 levels over time.
Your doctor may check your blood counts every year.
Your doctor may check your B12 levels every 2 to 3 years.
This is done to catch any problems early.
Low blood sugar is a risk when taken with insulin or other diabetes medicines.
Taking metformin along with insulin or certain other diabetes drugs raises the risk of low blood sugar.
These certain other diabetes drugs are ones that boost insulin release.
If you're on one of these combinations.
Triples: [["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "has administration instruction", "stop taking and call healthcare professional immediately if symptoms of lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "very weak and tired"], ["metformin", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "unusual muscle pain"], ["metformin", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "trouble breathing"], ["metformin", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "unusual sleepiness or sleep longer than usual"], ["metformin", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "unexplained stomach or intestinal problems with nausea and vomiting or diarrhea"], ["metformin", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "cold especially in arms and legs"], ["metformin", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "dizzy or lightheaded"], ["metformin", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "slow or irregular heartbeat"], ["metformin", "can cause", "vitamin b12 deficiency"], ["metformin", "has monitoring instruction", "check blood counts every year"], ["metformin", "has monitoring instruction", "check b12 levels every 2 to 3 years"], ["metformin", "has administration instruction", "check for problems early"], ["metformin", "increases risk of", "low blood sugar"], ["metformin", "interacts with", "insulin"], ["metformin", "interacts with", "other diabetes medicines"], ["metformin", "increases risk of low blood sugar when taken with", "insulin"], ["metformin", "increases risk of low blood sugar when taken with", "certain other diabetes drugs"], ["certain other diabetes drugs", "boost", "insulin release"], ["metformin", "has administration instruction", "if on one of these combinations"]]
Relations: ["boost", "can cause", "has administration instruction", "has monitoring instruction", "has serious side effect", "has symptom of lactic acidosis", "increases risk of", "increases risk of low blood sugar when taken with", "interacts with"]
Answer:

completion:
boost: The subject entity enhances or increases the activity or production of the object entity.  
can cause: The subject drug may lead to or result in the medical condition or effect specified by the object entity.  
has administration instruction: The subject drug requires the specific action or instruction specified by the object entity to be followed by the patient.  
has monitoring instruction: The subject drug requires the specific medical monitoring or testing specified by the object entity to be performed.  
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.  
has symptom of lactic acidosis: The subject drug may cause the specific symptom or set of symptoms associated with lactic acidosis specified by the object entity.  
increases risk of: The subject drug raises the likelihood of the medical condition or event specified by the object entity occurring.  
increases risk of low blood sugar when taken with: The subject drug raises the likelihood of low blood sugar when used in combination with the object entity.  
interacts with: The subject drug may have a pharmacological interaction or combined effect when used with the object entity.
